diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\dfrac{\dif \tilde \sQ}{\dif \tilde \P}\bigg|_{\tilde{\cev \gF}_t} &= \dfrac{\eta_0(\cev x_T)}{\eta_T(\cev x_0)} \exp\left(- \int_0^t \left(\eta_{T-s}^{-1}(\cev x_s) \tilde{\cev \gL} \eta_{T-s}(\cev x_s) \right) \dif s \right)
            &= \exp\left(- \int_0^t \left(\eta_{T-s}^{-1}(\cev x_s) \tilde{\cev \gL} \eta_{T-s}(\cev x_s) - \tilde{\cev \gL} \log \eta_{T-s}(\cev x_s) \right) \dif s \right)
where the last equality is by Dynkin's formula (\cref{thm:dynkin}).

issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Theorem A.7, the boundary ratio term \eta_0(\cev x_T)/\eta_T(\cev x_0) is replaced pathwise inside the exponential by \exp(\int_0^t \tilde{\cev \gL} \log \eta_{T-s}(\cev x_s) \dif s), citing Dynkin's formula. Dynkin's formula holds only for expectations, not almost surely along sample paths (the pathwise difference involves a non-trivial local martingale). Consequently, the stated expression for \dif\sQ/\dif\P has pathwise finite variation with no martingale/diffusion component, and its expectation under \P is strictly less than 1 whenever \eta \neq 1, meaning it is not a valid density process for any probability measure \sQ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the boundary factor \eta_{T-t}(\cev x_t)/\eta_T(\cev x_0) in the statement of Theorem A.7 for the Radon-Nikodym derivative \dif\sQ/\dif\P|_{\cev\gF_t} as given by the standard generalized Doob transform (Palmowski & Rolski, 2002, Theorem 4.2), and apply Dynkin's formula only when taking the expectation \E_\P[\log(\dif\P/\dif\sQ)] in Corollary A.9.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit pathwise formula for the Radon-Nikodym derivative \dif\sQ/\dif\P in Theorem A.7 is false. However, the true change-of-measure density includes the boundary factor, and Dynkin's formula can be legitimately applied under expectation in Corollary A.9, so the downstream KL divergence formulas and error bounds remain valid.
issues.title: Invalid pathwise Radon-Nikodym derivative via misapplied Dynkin's formula
issues.why_classification: A standard, local correction to the Radon-Nikodym derivative retains the endpoint ratio without altering the validity or advertised rates/forms of the subsequent KL divergence results (Corollary A.9, Corollary 3.5, Theorem 3.7).
